- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
854 3905 1253 Passcode: 116251 (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”

public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 854 3905 1253 Passcode: 116251.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MAY 4, 2021

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Combs, Lum, Martin,
  Munday, Romanelli, Brown Schachter, Scott,
  Varner

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Bouse, LA County Sheriff’s Department

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER
  12, 2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 12, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

A.  LETTER FROM RESIDENT REGARDING SPEED LIMITS ON CRENSHAW BLVD.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the Committee received a letter from a resident of the
condominiums at Silver Spur and Crenshaw Blvd. regarding concerns with speed limits on
Crenshaw Blvd.

The Committee did not agendize this item for future Traffic and Safety Committee meetings.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CITY HALL DRIVEWAY AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that Committee Member Brown Schachter requested that the City Hall exit at Palos Verdes
Drive North be reviewed due to concerns for pedestrian, bicycle, and equestrian traffic. A
suggestion was made to install warning signs at this location.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that collision reports showed six collisions east of
Crenshaw Blvd. and all were “rear end” type accidents; none involved bicyclists and none were
in the immediate vicinity of the City Hall driveway.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it does not appear that there is a need to address
collision concerns but there may be a for advanced warning signs. Signage and limit line options
were provided to the Committee.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Committee discuss this
item, receive public testimony and provide direction to staff regarding this matter.

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that the signs are very appropriate.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, May 4 ,2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE commented that there is a trail going through Masongate and
there is a crosswalk; it would be a good idea to add another crosswalk across the bridle trail at
this location.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that trimming back the shrub above near the mailbox may
help with visibility concerns.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she agrees with the shrubs being
trimmed back and the idea to continue the crosswalk. She stated that a sign is not necessary for
equestrians entering the driveway since they are able to see incoming traffic. She added that the
sign when exiting the driveway alerting to watch for pedestrians and bicyclists is a good idea, but
the sign for equestrians is not necessary. She also added that her concern is with the bicyclists
coming off the hill; the visibility for motorists exiting the driveway is blocked by the trees.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that he agrees and suggested that a sign be installed for
bicyclists travelling east on Palos Verdes Drive North, warning them to use caution when
approaching the driveway.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER agreed and stated that the suggestions discussed are a simple
way to fix an issue before it becomes an issue. He commented that he believes the signs would
be more visible than the limit lines.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN commented that it has been the philosophy of the City, if proposed signs
are not extremely helpful, that they be kept at a minimum because of visual pollution. This may
not be the case for this issue, but this may be a reason for the suggestions discussed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that he would be in favor or trimming or removing
the pepper tree that is blocking the pedestrian/bicycle trail on the west. He stated that he does
not like the idea of additional signs. He also agreed with trimming back the shrub behind the
mailbox.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that the pepper tree does not need to be removed;
removing the lower limbs of the pepper tree should suffice. He agrees with trimming back the
shrub behind the mailbox and adding an equestrian crosswalk. He does not agree with adding
signs.

There were no members of the public present.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT
to,
  REMOVE THE LOWER PORTION OF THE PEPPER TREE FOR CLEAR VISIBILITY OF
  THE BICYCLE TRAIL; TRIM THE SHRUB BEHIND THE MAILBOX FOR CLEAR
  VISIBILITY OF THE EQUESTRIAN TRAIL; AND, ADD A STOP LIMIT LINE AND
  CROSSWALK FOR THE EQUESTRIAN TRAIL.

AYES: Zuckerman, Boothe, Combs, Lum, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Brown Schachter, Scott,
  Varner

B.  DRAFT ENGINEERING AND TRAFFIC SURVEY

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that the Engineering and Traffic survey is a speed survey to establish speed limits on the
City’s streets. This is required by the State and is updated every five to seven years.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided an overview of the criteria used to determine the
speed limits, including: speed sampling, collision history, and conditions not readily apparent to
motorists. She also provided a table summarizing the recommended speed limits on the 24
roadway segments; there were no changes to existing speed limits in the draft recommended
speed limits. In addition, a table comparing the segment collision history of Deep Valley Drive and
Indian Peak Road was discussed.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, May 4 ,2021
 Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the Draft Engineering and Traffic Survey and receive public testimony.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLA inquired about when and how the street segments used in the
analysis were determined and also asked if these are still the best streets to analyze.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the streets are generally arterials and major
collectors; historically, they were chosen from a map identifying certain funding by the State
requiring an Engineering and Traffic Survey as part of the funding. She stated that other locations
have not been reviewed.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked if a residential street posted at 25 mph and was not part of the survey
could be a defense for someone who received a citation who does not believe they exceeded the
85th percentile. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki indicated the California Vehicle Code allows for
a “prima facie” posting for residential streets at 25 mph. Deputy Bouse confirmed this.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked if there would be an option for the Committee to suggest streets to
substitute. Director Wahba stated that this is likely a long-established list of roadways and
captures all the areas where radar enforcement is taking place. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that all of the City’s major streets are captured and stated that she will make a note of
considering other streets for the next update.

COMMITTEE BROWN SCHACHTER commented that the letter sent to the Traffic and Safety
Committee (AGENDA ITEM 4A), the roadway segment of concern is addressed in the
Engineering and Traffic Survey and it was determined that there is no need for a change. CHAIR
ZUCKERMAN suggested that a reply to the resident be prepared and it should include the
Engineering and Traffic survey findings.

There were no members of the public present.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE ENGINEERING AND TRAFFIC SURVEY AS PRESENTED AND TO
  FORWARD TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR ADOPTION.

AYES: Zuckerman, Boothe, Combs, Lum, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Brown Schachter, Scott,
  Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Wahba stated that the Engineering and Traffic Survey will be presented to the City
Council at their next meeting.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that on the south bound side of Montecillo intersecting
Aurora and Celeste, there has been a “stop” sign down, which need a metal post and
reinstallation.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that at the intersection at Silver Spur and Deep Valley
Drive, as you are making a left turn onto Silver Spur, there is overgrown vegetation making it
difficult to see vehicles coming from Crenshaw Blvd.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that in the median on Hawthorne Blvd. at the entry to Peninsula
Center (closest to the Habit restaurant), there is a sign that is down.

Director Wahba stated that staff will address these items.
